{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash --login

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -N 1
#   --partition=batch
#   -J ACE
#   -o /path/to/output.%J.out
#   -e /path/to/error.%J.err
#   --time=1:00:00
#   --mem=200G
#   --ntasks=1
#   --gres=gpu
#   --cpus-per-task=6

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  -c 6 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=1h \
  --queue=batch \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm %J using Flux job id.
exec >"/path/to/output.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"/path/to/error.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=200G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm job name (-J ACE) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module purge
module load gcc/11.1.0
conda activate realtime_ocl

cd ../../..

python main.py \
--dataset "cifar100" \
--batch_size 10 \
--lr 0.001 \
--lr_type "constant" \
--batch_delay 0 \
--gradient_steps 1 \
--output_dir "/path/to/tensorboard/output" \
--workers 4 \
--method "ACE" \
--seed 123 \
--size_replay_buffer 100
'
"
}
